title: imagebuildah: keep the job semaphore balanced when waitForStage's context is cancelled
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`waitForStage` gives up the stage goroutine's job-semaphore token while it polls another stage, then tries to take it back. If the build context is already cancelled — which is what happens when a remote `podman build` client drops — `Acquire` returns immediately without taking a token, even when one is free. The goroutine still `defer Release(1)`s, and `golang.org/x/sync/semaphore` panics:

    panic: semaphore: released more than held

When that executor is running inside `podman system service`, the panic kills the whole API server. Other in-flight remote builds on the same socket then die with `server probably quit: unexpected EOF`.

This reacquires the token with `context.Background()` on that path so the deferred Release stays balanced. It also returns an empty content summary if the stage's builder is already gone, which nil-derefs on the same cancel path (`getContentSummaryAfterAddingContent`).

#### How to verify it

```
go test -tags 'exclude_graphdriver_btrfs exclude_graphdriver_devicemapper containers_image_openpgp' ./imagebuildah \
  -run 'TestWaitForStageCancelledContextDoesNotOverRelease|TestWaitForStageAlreadyTerminatedKeepsToken|TestGetContentSummaryAfterAddingContentNilBuilder'
```

The cancelled-context test fails on main: after `waitForStage` returns, `TryAcquire(1)` succeeds, which means the caller no longer holds the token.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #7091

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

I hit this on Homebrew podman 6.1.1 (vendored buildah 1.45.0) serving several GitHub Actions slots through one user-scope API socket. Cancelling one build panicked the server and took down the others. The same code is still on main.

`Acquire(context.Background(), 1)` after a cancelled `Acquire` should not block in the usual case (we just released a token). If another stage grabbed it during the 10ms sleep, we wait for that stage's deferred Release; the build is already failing.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fix a panic (`semaphore: released more than held`) when a remote build is cancelled while waiting on another stage.
```

comments.body:
#7007 tweaks that part of the logic to use context.Background() when acquiring the semaphore so that it won't error out if the context was canceled - this error triggers more often in testing when the cancellation logic is properly wired up.
The new tests being added here in executor_test.go pass with its changes, and I'm not sure that it can still hit the case where the new guard in stage_executor.go would be necessary.
